description: Community-sourced tasks (competitions and public challenges) added on request; each record is a complete task manifest and the supplemental_paper record is their source collection.

supplemental_paper.name: Kaggle Santa 2025
supplemental_paper.title: Santa 2025 - Christmas Tree Packing Challenge (Kaggle competition)
supplemental_paper.authors: Kaggle competition organisers (metric and getting-started notebook)
supplemental_paper.access_status: competition pages read; metric and starter code taken from a public mirror pinned below

repositories.notes: Public mirror of the competition's metric notebook (santa-2025-metric.py), getting-started notebook (santa-2025-getting-started.py) and sample submission; used only to read the metric and to cross-check the reimplementation.

limitations: User-requested community supplement, outside the original 98-entry corpus; the source is a Kaggle competition, not a paper.
The competition pages are rendered client-side, so the metric was taken from a public mirror of the competition's metric notebook and cross-checked numerically against it.
Leaderboard values are not reproduced here; the reference value is the getting-started sample submission scored with the official metric.

tasks.name: Santa 2025: Christmas tree packing (n = 1..200)
tasks.description: For every n from 1 to 200 place n copies of the competition's fixed 15-vertex tree polygon (rotations allowed, no overlaps, coordinates within [-100, 100]) so that the bounding square of each configuration is as small as possible; the score is the sum over n of (bounding-square area / n), lower is better.

sources.locator: Competition overview and evaluation page (task statement, metric definition, submission format)
Getting-started notebook (tree geometry, collision rule, greedy sample submission)

requirements.datasets: None: the tree polygon is fixed and every configuration is constructed by the candidate.

evaluation.benchmark: Kaggle Santa 2025 - Christmas Tree Packing Challenge
evaluation.paper_metric: sum over n of bounding-square area / n

execution.interface: construct(n) -> array of shape (n, 3): rows (x, y, deg) for the n-tree configuration; called for every n in 1..200

limitations: The evaluator is an independent reimplementation of the competition metric (same polygon, scaling factor, overlap rule and bounding-square formula) and reproduces the official code's doctest value and the sample submission's score exactly; it is not the Kaggle scoring service.
No leaderboard value is embedded; the reference value is the getting-started sample submission (176.60550959158516).
